- Model consistently overestimates prices in early periods (especially first 5–10 days) and underestimates in later periods, suggesting a lag or delayed response to true market dynamics.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80+), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacting to recent highs.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts trend upward slowly but fail to capture sudden downward corrections or volatility clustering.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., <65), model tends to underestimate true values, especially when recent history is weak or volatile.
- Model shows poor calibration for multi-day price reversals — fails to adjust forecast slope when true outcome shows abrupt directional shifts.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture short-term volatility spikes or sudden drops, especially in mid-to-late horizon (e.g., 15–30 days).
- When true outcome shows a sharp downward trend after a peak, model continues upward or flattens, missing the turning point.
- Model underestimates true values when recent history includes multiple downward corrections — fails to recognize “recovery” or “rebound” patterns.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in high-price regimes — model assumes continuation of upward trend even when true outcome shows signs of cooling or reversal.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — forecasts are anchored to recent high values, even when true outcome shows clear downward momentum.
